newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE BONDS SLUMP, FIXED-RATE BONDS FALL MOST.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE BONDS SLUMP, FIXED-RATE BONDS FALL MOST.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished much lower Friday as fixed-rate bonds led a slump unleashed by sharp falls in U.S. Treasuries.
Traders put the declines wholly down to the shake-out in the U.S. Treasury market. Some players were taken aback by the sharp back up in U.S. yields.
"I do not fully understand why U.S. rates have risen so much. It may be fears in anticipation of U.S. indicators next week," said one bond market analyst.
Next week, U.S. July producer and consumer prices in addition to retail sales figures are due for release.
Argentina's Par Brady bond slumped one point to 73-1/2. Locally traded floating rate instruments were less affected but also fell.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was down $0.40 at 119.30.
Players said it was very difficult to predict where the Argentine market would go next week considering its tendency to follow the U.S. market.
"Next week we will continue to focus on U.S. treasury yields," said another trader.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield was last 11 basis points higher at 6.64 basis points.
In the money market, one-week peso BAIBOR, or Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, was at 6.9375 percent, down from 7.0625 percent.
